title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
slides: Why did OpenAI's board fire Sam Altman?
The board feared AI CEOs can't self-govern
That member says the problem remains unsolved
Boards should demand independent AI audits now
Ask your AI vendor who audits their safety claims
thread_text:
1. OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman. Why?

A sitting board member says the real reason wasn't a single scandal — it was that the board feared no AI CEO can credibly self-govern the technology. That fear remains unresolved today.

2. The conflict no one names.

A CEO who profits from shipping AI cannot also be the only check on its safety. The board knew this contradiction was structural — not a question of personal integrity, but of incentives.

3. That member says it's still unsolved.

A board member now admits the governance problem is exactly where it was. Nothing has been fixed since the crisis. And no independent structure has been built to replace the trust they lost.

4. Boards should demand independent audits.

Not self-assessments, not internal committees — third-party audits of safety claims, with real access to models and data. That is the only way a board can actually govern what it cannot see.

5. Ask your AI vendor today.

Who audits your safety claims? If the answer is an internal team, you do not have governance — you have a press release. Ask the question in your next vendor review.
